evidence.description: SPF and DMARC checks both failed, indicating unauthorized sender routing.
Display name claims to be 'Microsoft Security' while sender address is 'security@example.com' with mismatched reply-to and return-path domains.
Body link points to typosquatted domain 'micros0ft-login.example.xyz' masquerading as Microsoft login portal.
Image attachment contains a Microsoft logo and a QR code directing users to 'https://fake-login.example' to steal credentials.
Subject and body employ artificial urgency claiming password expiration today.

result.summary: The email impersonates Microsoft Security using urgency around password expiration to drive the recipient to credential phishing pages via both a typosquatted URL and a quishing QR code. Authentication checks (SPF/DMARC) fail, and sender routing contains conflicting domains.
result.recommended_action: Block the sender domain and associated URLs, quarantine the message across the mail environment, and remind the user not to scan embedded QR codes or submit credentials.
